arguments: Clone failure path may release using a caller-controlled handle pointer after allocator-mutated output state
message.text: Clone failure path may release using a caller-controlled handle pointer after allocator-mutated output state

properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: invalid because the allocator rejects any non-invalid seeded handle and, on success, always writes a fresh handle before the clone-failure release path can run. Evidence: clone copies in_vec[1] into p_handle then calls allocation and only releases after allocation success and clone failure at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_hash.c:238, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_hash.c:241, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_hash.c:247, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_hash.c:249; the allocator rejects nonzero handles at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:89 and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:90, and writes *handle = i + 1 before returning success at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:110 and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:112. Gap: none.
properties.mitigation: Do not initialize p_handle from untrusted input unless the allocator contract requires a validated client-provided placeholder. Prefer allocating a fresh target handle into a local temporary initialized to an invalid value, copy it to out_vec[0] only after successful allocation/clone, and release only the fresh handle known to have been allocated in this call.
properties.reasoning: The clone path seeds the output handle from a value read out of in_vec[1].base, passes the same pointer to the allocator, and on clone failure releases whatever handle value is then stored at p_handle. If tfm_crypto_operation_alloc does not always overwrite p_handle before returning success, or if the client-controlled seed is interpreted as meaningful by the allocator/release APIs, a clone failure could release an unintended existing operation handle. This file does not show allocator semantics, so the issue is a cross-component lifetime candidate rather than a confirmed bug, but the local pattern couples untrusted handle input, allocation, and release-by-pointer in a way that can produce state confusion.
